widget.instructions: The diagram shows circular motion; in a vertical circle the speed changes as the stone climbs.

args.text: Check the top first: the string stays taut only if mv²/R ≥ mg there.

stem: A small stone on a light string of length {{R}} m is whirled in a vertical circle. Take g = 9.8 m/s².
What is the least speed it must have at the bottom so that the string stays taut all the way round?

hints.text: At the top, the least speed makes the tension zero: gravity alone gives the centripetal force.

loop-top-condition.text: √(gR) is the least speed at the top. The stone loses speed climbing 2R, so it needs more at the bottom.

loop-zero-top.text: At the top the stone can't be at rest: the string would go slack. It needs at least √(gR) there.

dimension-mismatch.text: Check the unit: the answer is a velocity.

workedSolution.text: At the top: mg = mv_top²/R, so v_top² = gR.
Energy: v_bottom² = gR + 4gR = 5gR, so v = √(5 × 9.8 × {{R}}) = {{ans}} m/s.

loop-top-condition.front: Minimum speed at the bottom of a vertical circle on a string?
loop-top-condition.back: √(5gR): √(gR) at the top plus the energy for the 2R climb.

loop-zero-top.front: Can a body on a string be at rest at the top of a vertical circle?
loop-zero-top.back: No: the string would go slack. It needs at least √(gR) there.
